# Urban Economics & the Value of Location {#sec-econ}

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
## Anchor: Singapore
**Dataset** — [HDB Resale Flat Prices](https://data.gov.sg/collections/189/view) (data.gov.sg): every public-housing resale transaction since 1990 — roughly a million sales with flat type, floor area, storey, and crucially **remaining lease** — under the Singapore Open Data Licence, no login or key; geocodable via the free [OneMap API](https://www.onemap.gov.sg/apidocs/) (free registration). Eighty percent of Singaporeans live in HDB flats, so this is a near-census of a housing market. *Verified June 2026.*
:::

Why do cities exist at all, and why does a square meter cost ten times more in one place than another? Singapore — a city-state that planned its way to prosperity, where the state built the housing and the market prices it — anchors the economist's toolkit. Its resale dataset is a teaching miracle: complete, clean, thirty-five years deep, and containing a variable (lease decay on 99-year flats) that turns abstract present-value theory into a regression you can run.

## Why cities exist: agglomeration

Sharing, matching, learning; agglomeration economies as the force scaling laws measure from the outside (@sec-scaling); the equilibrium tug-of-war with congestion and rent.

## Land and location: bid-rent

Von Thünen to Alonso; estimating Singapore's price–distance gradient from the CBD; polycentricity as the gradient's empirical complication.

## Hedonic regression: pricing the unpriceable

The hedonic framework done properly (extending @sec-stats): floor premiums, MRT proximity, and the clean estimation of lease decay; capitalization as a general instrument for valuing public goods.

## Housing policy in the data

Public housing at national scale; the Ethnic Integration Policy and what transaction data reveal about engineered desegregation (a counterpoint to @sec-abm); cooling measures as natural experiments (@sec-causal returns).

## The economic complexity of cities

From products to industries to skills: relatedness, the industry space, and measuring what a city knows how to do.

::: {.callout-note}
## Theory sidebar (planned)
**The isolated state, downtown** — von Thünen's 1826 rings of agriculture and Alonso's 1964 translation to the city: how a model of cabbage transport became the foundation of urban land economics.
:::
